reference.label: WHO reference level: 100 Bq/m³, 300 at most

source.citation: WHO national radon survey (Global Health Observatory indicator RADON_Q302, 2019 and 2021 rounds); Gaskin J, et al. Global estimate of lung cancer mortality attributable to residential radon. Environ Health Perspect 2018;126:057009, Table 1.
source.licence: WHO data policy; EHP open access

caveats: Surveys differ in design and year; a national figure hides large local differences (geology, building type).
Countries without a representative survey are left blank, and so are countries whose reported figures contradict each other: Peru, Poland, Paraguay, Turkmenistan.

excluded.POL: WHO survey answer inconsistent (arithmetic mean 40, geometric mean 100); Gaskin geometric mean 133 above the WHO survey arithmetic mean 40
excluded.TKM: WHO survey answer inconsistent (arithmetic mean 200, geometric mean 200)
excluded.PRY: Gaskin geometric mean 21 above the WHO survey arithmetic mean 5.5
excluded.PER: Gaskin geometric mean 24 above the WHO survey arithmetic mean 22
